TL:DR; Good game, very buggy, Very fun CO-OP game, mandatory stealth alone.

A genuinely fun game that's been getting a pretty bad wrap of late due to its relationship with its publishers and a development cycle on a team that can't really juggle both making new things as well as balancing and bugfixes since their different teams are also their own bugfixers.

But I'm not really here to be a mouthpiece, nor do I think the amount of anger is entirely justified. People were praising the game over the Triple A releases but the moment the successful game downticks they treat it just the same. At least the devs are taking it to heart and trying to improve, but ♥♥♥♥ takes time, so I'll cut them that break.

Most of my gameplay stuff will be related to running on 8-9 as that's the difficulties I am mostly on these days (During the period of increased spawnrate changes). So just keep that in mind.

On a gameplay perspective, I think the game is generally very fun. I have been able to put so many hours in to it because there is enough variation that you can do with different stratagem compositions, which ultimately end up in how you play the game. 
     The difficulties also drastically change your combat approaches. On lower levels you can be way more gungho, while on higher difficulties you do have to try avoid just alerting all of the map to your presence. I really love the stealth mechanics in the game and will often try to set up ambushes and kill boxes.

Maybe you go for a meta comp of a support weapon, backpack, and two offensive strikes like an orbital and an airstrike, or you do silly stuff like bringing a full set of orbital strikes and raining hell (mostly on your allies). What you do can make you a specific, vital role in the party like "the anti-tank" who's entire shtick is just handling heavy foes whilst some nimble ♥♥♥♥♥♥ runs around closing bugholes. I found doling roles like that is very helpful on higher level missions where stratagems are often limited. Either way, I like working from a base template and specializing.

On a negative side, I do find that the gun meta is a little annoying to deal with. The intent is that you use your full set of weaponry to deal with your threats, but there are just so many weapons not worth bringing at all. I understand you can't just positively buff all guns, but more needs to be done to make worse guns more viable (Why would I bring the Liberator penetrator when the Adjudicator does the same, and still isn't a very great gun?). 

Limitations on orbital strikes are also not a fun modifier for higher end gameplay. Being unable to rely on orbital strikes because they scatter just means the one of 3 options you have (if you are -also- playing with the reduced stratagem limit modifier) has gone to waste, or worse yet, killed a teammate / blocked you / ally's exit. 

I hope they do something to the effect of "Orbitals have increased/decreased" radius rather than just being pure RNG if it'll hit where you put it. Knowing something might airburst wider can both be a detriment and a reason for bringing a particular thing, where as knowing it can miss is just a reason not to bring it.

Helldivers 2 is a game I want to love. The tongue-in-cheek lore, the obvious parodies of democratic and authoritarian tropes, the co-op gameplay with tons of cool weapons and strategems to play with, all make it a very enjoyable experience...

Is what I would have said, before all this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. 

This game built TONS of goodwill, with its responsive dev team, regular updates and Freemium payout structure that isn't predatory by nature. Yes, there are bugs, but with a little teamwork, and some friendly fire, most of those could be dealt with or avoided entirely, and the gameplay more than made up for it. 

I don't think I've EVER seen a company burn so much goodwill, so fast, as Sony did with Helldivers 2. I don't think I've seen a misstep as terrible, a blunder as catastrophic, since EA's Star Wars Battlefront 2. The only reason this burnt more goodwill is because EA hasn't had goodwill from its fans for a long time. 

We thought Sony had listened to us, when we told them to piss off, forcing us to make PSN accounts to play. We were wrong. They retaliated against their fans by region-locking Helldivers from non-PSN supporting regions of the world. People who payed money to buy their game, now robbed of both their time and money. 

Beyond the real world implications, this massively impacts the ability of Joel and Arrowhead to manage their game, setting missions that are now well beyond the abilities of those helldivers who remain. This drives even more away. 

I was there at Malevelon Creek. I fought with my brothers for managed democracy, through the automaton hordes. I was looking forward to crushing a potential third enemy with my brothers in arms. 

Little did I know that the enemy would turn out to be the people sending us out there in the first place. 

The devs didn't deserve this. The Helldivers didn't deserve this. The players who live in other countries didn't deserve this. 

To the SONY corpos responsible for ruining Helldivers for so many, for dividing us and casting our brothers to the wayside, from the bottom of my democracy loving heart:

Find one of the ICBMs, lost and forlorn on a bug-infested world, and sit on the tip. Line your pucker up with the tip of that rocket, and let the thrusters shove it so far up your rectum that your skin plasters to the warhead.

One of those games where I wish I could leave a mixed review.

I have never had so much fun in a multiplayer game in a while. The sheer chaos and destruction quenches the soul. The strategems make you feel powerful. Like some war god out for blood trying to rid the galaxy of anything that isn't human. Extremely fun.

Unfortunately on the other hand once that dopamine hit starts becoming less and less impactful, the game just feels very very repetitive. Somewhat grindy as well. While the different planets are interesting and beautiful at first, making me want to explore every corner, the wonder wears off after a while and it just becomes "do same objective but weather different now".

I hope they don't squander this success they had and leave the game in the dust like many companies do nowadays. New content and maps are a must. Would love to use these weapons bestowed upon us in different settings. Perhaps a map where you play in a large city with some destructible buildings. Or a map set on a massive facility floating on water. Just some examples off the top of my head.

All that said I would only recommend this game when it's on a good discount and you have friends to play it with. Otherwise give it a year or two when the developers have whatever their vision is up and running. I shall be watching their careers with great interest and hopefully in the future I can set my review to positive.
